topic.name: The Average Rate of Change of a Function

question.text: A leaky pool is losing water. The amount of water lost after $t$ hours is given by the expression $t^2 - t + 3$ gallons, where $t \geq 0.$ What is the average rate of water loss over the first twelve hours?
question.explanation:
Let $f(t)= t^2 - t + 3$ be the amount of water lost in gallons after $t$ hours. To find the average rate of change of $f(t)$ from $t=0$ to $t=12,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[0,12]{:}$

\[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta t} &= \dfrac { f(b) - f(a)}{b-a} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac { f(12) - f(0)}{12-0}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac { \left[(12)^2 - (12) + 3\right] - \left[(0)^2 - (0) + 3\right] }{12}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac { 135 - 3 } {12} \\[5pt] & = 11 } \] Therefore, the average rate of water loss is $11$ gallons per hour.

example.title: Calculating the Average Rate of Change: Word Problem

question.text: Suppose that $s(t) = 2t^3 - t$ represents the position of a race car along a straight track, measured in feet from the starting line at $t$ seconds. What is the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t = 1$ to $t = 3?$
question.explanation:
Let $s(t)=2t^3-t$ be the position of the race car in feet after t seconds. To find the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t=1$ to $t=3,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[1,3]{:}$ \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{\Delta s}{\Delta t} &= \dfrac { s(b) - s(a)}{b-a} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac { s(3) - s(1)}{3-1}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac { \left[2(3)^3 - (3)\right] - \left[2(1)^3 -(1)\right] }{2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac { 51 - 1 } {2} \\[5pt] & = 25.\\ } \]

Therefore, the average rate of change of $s(t)$ is $25$ feet per second.

example.title: Calculating the Average Rate of Change: Word Problem

question.text:
Find an interval where the average rate of change of $f(x)$ equals $0$ given the following table of values of $f(x)\mathbin{:}$

$ x $ $\,1\,$ $\,2\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,4\,$ $\,5\,$ $\,6\,$ $\,7\,$
$ f(x) $ $\,-2\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,-1\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,-4\,$ $\,3\,$ $\,5\,$
question.explanation:
We have $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}=0$ if and only if $\Delta f = 0.$ So \begin{align*} & \Delta f = 0 \\ & f(b)-f(a) = 0 \\ & f(b)=f(a). \end{align*}

This means we have to find an interval $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(2)=f(6)=3,$ we conclude that $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}= 0$ on the interval $[2,6].$
